title: When All Context Matters: Extended Cache Augmented Generation - Luis Romero-Sevilla, Orbis
talk_summary: The talk compares RAG, GraphRAG, and 'cache augmented generation' (CAG) for a scenario where all documents are relevant and frequently replaced, proposing parallel CAG buckets with a supervisor model interrogating each. It is a conceptual architecture sketch with no benchmarks, no implementation details, and no cost numbers.

takeaways.technique: Parallel KV-cache buckets with supervisor interrogation
takeaways.what_they_do: Split a large corpus across multiple large-context models, cache each KV matrix, and have a stronger supervisor model query each bucket and synthesize an answer, asking follow-ups to specific buckets when interesting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what if we use more CAGs in parallel and distribute the documents across different context buckets

takeaways.technique: Avoid domain-based sharding; balance by document count
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately distribute documents in no particular order, only balancing counts, because a supervisor tends to skip domains that look irrelevant at first glance.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the supervisor tends to ignore domains that at first glance seem irrelevant

takeaways.what_they_do: They acknowledge KV cache is expensive and say cost can be reduced by optimizing how long each cache lives, without giving specifics.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there are ways to reduce that cost by optimizing how long each cache lives
